prepared_outreach.subject: Research inquiry concerning Cairo CG 53469 / JE 35425 (gold phallus sheath from Mendes)
prepared_outreach.body_en:
Dear Egyptian Museum Collections/Conservation Team,

I am conducting non-invasive provenance and object-history research on Cairo CG 53469 / JE 35425, catalogued by Vernier as an 'Enveloppe de phallus' from the 1902 Mendes (Tell Ibn es-Salam) burial associated with Nesbanebdjedet.

Could you please confirm whether CG 53469 / JE 35425 is currently held by the Egyptian Museum in Tahrir, or whether it has been transferred to another museum or storage facility? If possible, I would be grateful for any current object record, current mass and dimensions, and modern photographs showing the front, reverse, sides and especially the crumpled basal area.

I would also like to ask whether the object has ever been examined by radiography, CT/micro-CT, XRF, microscopy, or 3D imaging, and whether its conservation history records any internal packing, support, residues, removed material, seams, joins, folded edges, or a separately attached basal component. If such imaging or conservation documentation exists, access to the relevant report, image, or reference number would be extremely helpful.

If no internal imaging has yet been performed, I would be interested to know whether a strictly non-destructive radiographic or CT examination could be considered by the museum's conservation/research staff. The purpose is to distinguish collapsed gold sheet or conservation support from any discrete ancient internal material; no destructive sampling is requested.

Thank you very much for your time and for any guidance you can provide.
